heroHeadline: White House Withdraws ICE Director Nominee as DHS Touts 16 Months of Zero Border Releases
heroSubtitle: The White House withdrew Lance Schroyer's nomination to lead ICE on Sept 17, 2026 after Sen. Rand Paul withheld a confirmation hearing pending answers on civilian deaths during ICE operations, leaving the agency without a Senate-confirmed director since the Obama era. A day earlier, ICE confirmed that an enforcement surge around Indianapolis first reported in early September was 'Operation Safe Community — Indiana,' a five-day operation that netted 426 arrests, while DHS separately announced 16 consecutive months of zero Border Patrol releases at the southern border. On Sept 18, ICE officer Christian Castro — charged in the January Minneapolis shooting of Julio Cesar Sosa-Celis during Operation Metro Surge — pleaded not guilty to federal charges of lying to the FBI about the incident, becoming the first federal officer charged over that operation. The 287(g) local-police deputization program grew to 2,510 active agreements as of Sept 15.
